raw_response:
I am already old, so I do not want to toss things around too much. I have 25.1 mu, not a big farm, and only two people in the house, so this year I will still follow the wheat-maize rotation the way we know well. I finished middle school, so I can listen to the extension station and compare it with my own field experience, but in the end I still trust what has worked on my land. Wheat is the main crop to hold steady yield, so I will not save too much on base fertilizer. If I cut too hard and the seedlings come up weak, later it is hard to make it back. Maize after wheat has a very tight window, so I will keep it simple: harvest wheat, do light field preparation, and sow maize quickly. I have well water, so if spring is dry I will water wheat at the key stages, and for maize I will give one irrigation if the rain is short around tasseling. I will not chase very high yield this year; at my age, steady production and not spending too much cash is more important.
